in_hebrew.name: אפיפניה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אפיפניה נגזר מהמילה היוונית 'אפיפניה', שפירושה הופעה או התגלות. בהקשר הנוצרי, השם מתייחס להתגלותו של אלוהים בבשר, דהיינו, לידתו של ישו המשיח. השם משמש גם כזכר לחג ההתגלות הנוצרי, הנחגג ב-6 בינואר, ומציין את ביקורם של חכמי המזרח אצל ישו התינוק.

in_greek.name: Επιφάνεια
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Επιφάνεια προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'επιφάνεια', που σημαίνει εμφάνιση ή εκδήλωση. Στο χριστιανικό πλαίσιο, το όνομα αναφέρεται στην εκδήλωση του Θεού στο肉, δηλαδή, στη γέννηση του Ιησού Χριστού. Το όνομα χρησιμοποιείται επίσης ως ανάμνηση της χριστιανικής γιορτής της Επιφάνειας, που γιορτάζεται στις 6 Ιανουαρίου και σηματοδοτεί τη επίσκεψη των Μάγων στο βρέφος Ιησού.

in_latin.name: Epiphania
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Epiphania derivatum est ex voce Graeca 'ἐπιφάνεια', quae apparitionem seu manifestationem significat. In contextu christiano, nomen refertur ad manifestationem Dei in carne, scilicet, ad nativitatem Jesu Christi. Nomen etiam commemorat festum christianum Epiphaniae, quod die 6 Januarii celebratur et visitationem Magorum ad infantem Jesum notat.

in_english.name: Epiphania
in_english.meaning: Manifestation of God, appearance of divine
in_english.long_meaning: The name Epiphania is derived from the Greek word 'ἐπιφάνεια', meaning manifestation or appearance. In Christian context, it refers to the manifestation of God in the flesh, namely, the birth of Jesus Christ. The name also commemorates the Christian feast of Epiphany, celebrated on January 6th, marking the visit of the Magi to the infant Jesus. The name symbolizes spiritual awakening, divine revelation, and the embodiment of faith. Historically, it signifies the recognition of Jesus as the Son of God by the Gentiles.

saint_reference.note: Epiphania of Milan was a 4th-century Christian saint.

data.cultural_impact: The Feast of Epiphany, also known as the Twelfth Night or Three Kings' Day, is celebrated annually on January 6th or the closest Sunday. It commemorates the visit of the three Magi, or Wise Men, to the infant Jesus, whom they acknowledged as the King of Kings and the Son of God. Epiphany is a significant day in various Christian cultures, and the traditions surrounding it can include exchanging gifts, feasting, and processions with colorful floats representing the Magi. These practices promote unity, joy, and community spirit in many Christian communities around the world.
data.spiritual_significance: Epiphany holds immense spiritual significance as it celebrates the culmination of Christ's incarnation and the revealing of God's message to the world through the Magi. As the manifestation of the divine, Epiphany reminds us that God actively engages with humanity, guiding us towards a deeper and more profound understanding of our faith. It is a reminder that the journey towards realizing the truth of God's love and purpose for our lives is a continuous process, as we too can have our very own 'Epiphany' moments in life, illuminating our path towards greater wisdom, awareness, and transformation.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Epiphania remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: Grace Epiphania from Athens, Greece embodies the meaning of Epiphania - "Manifests as a divine revelation". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Epiphania signifies a revelation or manifestation of God, symbolizing the moment when the true nature of Christ was first made known to the Gentiles through the visit of the Magi. It captures the essence of divine illumination and the profound realization of God's presence in our lives.
